title: systematic-load-profiles-and-scaling-experiments-2026
author: Nora Chen
content:
Overview:

## Purpose
This playbook documents a repeatable, engineering-focused approach to construct, run, and interpret end-to-end load and scaling experiments for the Redwood serving runtime. The goal is to give engineers a single, well-scoped procedure for validating autoscaling policies, kernel scheduling knobs, KV cache warmup behavior, and cost/latency tradeoffs across realistic workload shapes.

## Scope and when to use this doc
- Validating autoscaler configuration changes prior to a production rollout.
- Quantifying latency vs. cost impact of new kernel scheduling heuristics.
- Reproducing and debugging SLO regressions tied to workload distribution shifts.
- Benchmarking model-variants or quantization profiles under mixed concurrency.

## High-level experiment design
1. Define the hypothesis (explicit). Example: "Adaptive batching with max_batch=64 reduces 95th percentile latency by >=15% for short-sequence chat workloads at 300 qps."
2. Select a small set of representative traffic profiles (see Profiles table).
3. Establish stable baseline (3 successful runs with current config).
4. Apply change under test.
5. Re-run identical experiment suite and collect telemetry.
6. Analyze deltas against baseline using the analysis checklist below.

## Representative traffic profiles (canonicalized)
| Profile name | Composition | Avg seq len | Burst pattern | Target qps | Notes |
|--------------|-------------|------------:|---------------|----------:|-------|
| Chat-short   | 85% chat + 15% system prompts | 96 tokens | Poisson bursts, CV=1.2 | 300 | Typical webchat PLG use-case
| Assist-long  | 40% long-form completions | 1024 tokens | Steady ramp with periodic spikes | 40 | Notebook / code gen workloads
| Embedding-burst | 100% embedding (batchable) | 1 token | High-frequency microbursts (100ms inter-arrival) | 400 | Tests batching & coalescing
| Mixed-enterprise | 60% chat, 20% completion, 20% embeddings | variable | Diurnal with hourly spikes | 120 | Representative enterprise route mix

## Pre-experiment checklist
- Owner: assign an experiment lead and a verifier.
- Environment: use a non-production cluster matching the target capacity profile (same GPU generation & kernel build).
- Config snapshot: save current model.json, kernel-mapper.yaml, autoscaler policy JSON, and routing rules. Example:

Save command examples:
```
kubectl -n runtime get configmap kernel-mapper -o yaml > kernel-mapper.prechange.yaml
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-experiments/configs/model.json model.json.prechange
```

- Monitoring hooks: ensure traces, per-token cost, and KV cache hit-rate metrics are enabled. Required metrics:
  - runtime.request.latency.p50/p95/p99
  - kernel.queue.depth, kernel.active_batches
  - kvcache.hit_rate, kvcache.evicts
  - gpu.utilization, gpu.memory.used
  - autoscaler.desired_replicas, autoscaler.actual_replicas

## Execution steps (detailed)
1. Baseline run
   - Deploy a tagged Canary stack: runtime image tag = stable/2026-01-12-canary
   - Warmup KV cache: replay 20,000 representative prefixes at production token distribution.
   - Duration: run steady-state for 30 minutes plus a 10-minute spike window.
   - Run 3 trials separated by 15 minutes idle.
2. Change under test
   - Apply change (examples: kernel scheduling policy flip, max_batch increase, new quantization kernel).
   - Restart runtime nodes using rolling restart with 1 node at a time.
   - Repeat warmup and trials as for baseline.
3. Safety guardrails during runs
   - Abort if p99 latency exceeds baseline p99 by 2x or absolute p99 > 5s for > 60s.
   - If GPU OOM occurs, collect node logs and capture heap/profile then revert.

## Data collection and artifact list
- Raw telemetry (Prometheus TSDB snapshot) for window start..end.
- Traces: sampled 1:50 with full token span for at least 10% of requests.
- Kernel executor logs and per-kernel timing histograms.
- Autoscaler event log and provisioning timeline.
- Workload generator logs (k6/Locust) and input request corpus.
- Cost estimate: GPU-hours * on-demand cost + estimated inference token cost.

Create an artifacts folder naming convention: experiments/<YYYYMMDD>-<profile>-<change>/

## Analysis checklist
- Verify experiment parity: identical request corpus and seed across baseline and variant runs.
- Primary checks (pass/fail):
  - p95 improved/worsened (quantify absolute ms and percent).
  - p99 behavior during spikes.
  - Mean GPU utilization delta.
  - KV cache hit-rate delta and warmup time.
  - Autoscaler oscillation or thrash events.
- Secondary checks:
  - Per-model token cost changes.
  - Number of kernel preemptions or queue overflows.
  - Any increase in tail queue depth indicating head-of-line blocking.

## Typical experiment failure modes and remediations
- Observation: p99 improves at steady-state but regresses during spike.
  Remediation: reduce max_batch or enable fast-path for short-sequence requests.
- Observation: autoscaler overshoots and causes thrash.
  Remediation: increase stabilization window and add rate limit to scale-up.
- Observation: KV cache hit-rate drops after change.
  Remediation: review shard placement, increase warmup traffic, or adjust cache eviction policy.

## Quick reference: CLI snippets
k6 synthetic profile example (chat-short):
```
k6 run --vus 40 --duration 30m --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086/chat-short.js
```
Locust swarm with custom payload:
```
locust -f locustfile.py --headless -u 300 -r 50 --run-time 30m
```
Extract prom snapshot:
```
kubectl -n monitoring exec prometheus-0 -- promtool snapshot /prom/data /tmp/snapshot.tar.gz
kubectl cp prometheus-0:/tmp/snapshot.tar.gz ./artifacts/snapshot.tar.gz
```

## Config matrix (example)
| Variable | Baseline | Variant A | Variant B | Notes |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| max_batch | 32 | 64 | 16 | Larger batch reduces per-token overhead but increases latency for short seqs
| kernel-map | default | priority-driven | numa-aware | Kernel mapping strategy to GPUs
| autoscaler.min_replicas | 2 | 2 | 4 | Minimum pool size
| autoscaler.scale_up_window_s | 60 | 120 | 30 | Stability vs responsiveness

## Reporting template (what to publish after an experiment)
- Title: short, change under test, profile name, date
- One-paragraph summary of outcome (latency vs cost tradeoff).
- Key metrics table (baseline vs variant): p50/p95/p99, GPU util, cost estimate, cache hit-rate.
- Graphs: latency heatmap, kernel-level time series, autoscaler timeline.
- Action items: accept / iterate / rollback / require more tests.

## Ownership and escalation
- Experiment owner: runtime performance engineer (assign in doc frontmatter).
- Verifier: senior SRE or runtime tech lead.
- Escalate to oncall if incident occurs during run (follow oncall runbook link).

## Appendix: reproducible artifacts and example corpus format
- Request corpus JSON schema (newline-delimited):
```
{"route":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"rwd-small-v2","prompt":"<...>","max_tokens":256,"seed":42}
```
- Acceptable image: a timeline diagram text description: "Diagram shows warmup -> steady-state -> spike -> cooldown with autoscaler adjusting replicas at t+8m".
